features.name: counter_argument_count
features.definition: How many counter-argument comments are in the discussion's available list?
features.spec: import json; parse df['OC_comments'] as a JSON list; return len(list). Return null if missing or not parseable as a list; empty list gives 0. Counts comments, not distinct commenters.

h0: counter_argument_count has no association with the likelihood that the OP changed their view.
h1: Higher counter_argument_count is associated with a higher likelihood of the OP changing their view (fewer responses, lower likelihood).
note: "Fewer" is operationalized as a lower count of comments in OC_comments, tested linearly. The supplied list is "available" comments and may be a filtered subset of all replies. It may include comments that led to or followed a delta, so the count could be tied to the outcome. List length counts comments, not distinct commenters. This is an association only. The hypothesis says "original argument contains" responses; the responses come from OC_comments, not the argument text.
